title: You can say where the grid starts and how fine it may get
goal: The grid always starts at the corner of the picture and always uses the same spacing, so it cannot be lined up with what is already in a screenshot. Add two things. First, a smallest cell setting, so you can say the grid never goes finer than four points, or eight, or whatever the work needs. Second, a way to say where the grid starts: a mode where two lines, one across and one down, mark the zero point, and you move them with the arrow keys or by dragging, with the same pull to edges that dragging a layer already has. While you are placing them the tool bar becomes a small bar with Cancel and Done and the smallest cell slider, so the whole adjustment is in one place. Return accepts, Escape puts it back the way it was.
notes: Raised and unblocked on 2026-09-05: the user asked for this a second time and is waiting on it, so it no longer waits behind the other grid tasks. Also asked that zooming in and out during the mode be a way to change the cell size, alongside the slider. Asked for by the user on 2026-09-05, after the canvas grid shipped. Today CanvasGridSettings (PhotonzCore/CanvasGrid.swift) carries isVisible, axes, spacing and majorEvery, with a spacing range of 1 to 512, and no origin at all, so the grid is anchored to the document corner. Add an origin point and a minimum cell size to those settings, both in the same store (CanvasGridStore, app wide rather than per document, behind next-canvas-grid). The level of detail ladder must respect the minimum: it currently picks rungs purely from zoom, so it needs a floor. The confirm bar has a pattern to copy rather than invent: the crop tool already replaces the canvas chrome with a two button bar (EditorView.cropActionBar around line 1436, Cancel and Crop, wired to Escape and Return), and the user is describing the same shape with a slider added. Reuse the modal state handling crop uses so two modes cannot both be live. Snapping for the two lines should call the same entry point a layer drag calls, and this task should be ordered after the-grid-is-always-behind-the-canvas-and-things so resize snapping and grid snapping exist before another thing wants to snap. The mode is a new visible surface; the user asked for it directly, so no decision card is needed, but if the runner wants to change the shape of the bar it should ask rather than guess.
acceptance: The grid settings gain a smallest cell size, typed, and the grid never draws finer than it however far you zoom in
A command puts the canvas into grid adjustment: two lines appear at the current zero point, one across and one down, clearly different from the grid itself
The lines move by dragging and by the arrow keys, one step per press and a larger step with Shift, and they pull to layer edges and canvas edges the way a dragged layer does
While adjusting, the tool bar is replaced by a bar holding Cancel, Done and the smallest cell slider, and the canvas shows the grid updating live as the slider moves
Return leaves the mode keeping the change, Escape leaves it putting back the zero point and the cell size that were there before, and clicking Done or Cancel does the same
Everything else on the canvas is left alone while adjusting: no layer can be selected, moved or edited by accident
The zero point is remembered with the other grid settings, and a grid that has never been adjusted sits exactly where it does today
Core logic covered by tests in PhotonzCore written before the implementation, including that an offset grid still lands on whole positions at every zoom
Audit written under queue/audits/ with pictures of the mode, the two lines caught on a layer edge, and the grid before and after, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: adversarial review, before building. (1) Entry point: a menu item alone would never be found. The place a person is already standing when they care about the grid is the Grid section of the inspector, so the mode is entered from a button there AND from View > Grid, not from a menu only. (2) Dragging: hit-testing a one point line is fiddly, so pressing ANYWHERE on the canvas moves the zero point to the pointer and keeps it under the pointer for the rest of the drag. One rule, no invisible hit targets, and the lines are always exactly where you last pressed. (3) Arrow keys reuse the layer nudge (1pt, 10pt with shift) so the step is the one already in the fingers. (4) The mode snapshots the WHOLE grid settings on entry, so it can switch the grid on for you (nobody adjusts a grid they cannot see) and Escape still puts everything back. (5) Cut from the mock reading: no separate crosshair badge or draggable handles. Added: the bar shows the zero point as numbers, because you cannot check that 0,0 landed on 24,16 by eye. (6) Smallest cell is a floor on what is DRAWN, not on the pull, which is what the acceptance says; that combination is the useful one (pull on 1pt, look at 8pt cells) but it is worth asking the user, so it goes in the audit as a question.

decided without a card (no visible consequence to weigh): smallest cell raises the BASE of the level of detail ladder to max(spacing, smallest cell) rather than skipping rungs, so the cells you see are still whole multiples of the spacing and the ladder keeps stacking. Default smallest cell is 1pt, i.e. no floor, so a grid nobody has touched draws exactly what it draws today.

core (TDD, tests first): CanvasGridSettings gains origin and minimumCell, both Codable with defaults so a stored grid reads back unchanged; drawnSpacing = max(spacing, minimumCell) is the base of the level of detail ladder; CanvasGridLevels.levels takes minimumCell and .lines takes an origin and counts whole steps from it; Snapping.snapFrameOrigin and .snapResizedFrame take a gridOrigin and quantize from it; new CanvasGridOriginAdjustment holds the snapshot plus the live copy; CanvasGridOriginLabel formats the readout. 21 new tests, 3327 green.

app: EditorState owns the placement session (begin/move/nudge/setGridMinimumCell/commit/cancel) and drawnCanvasGrid returns the live grid while placing, so the lines redraw under the markers. CanvasNSView draws the two markers in the accent above the grid and below the snap guide, takes every mouse and key event while placing (press anywhere moves the zero point, arrows nudge 1pt and 10pt with shift, Return keeps, Escape puts back), keeps a crosshair over the whole canvas, and draws the yellow guide when the point catches an edge. EditorView replaces the tool bar with a bar holding the readout, the smallest cell slider, Cancel and Done. Entry from the Canvas section Starts at button and View > Set Grid Origin.

verified live with Scripts/playtest/grid-origin-walk.json on the probe (Screen Recording granted, real captures): enter the mode, press to place, drag onto the rectangle corner and catch it at 620,420 with guides showing, arrow nudges to 622,431 including a shift step of ten, Done keeps it, smallest cell 16 typed in the panel still draws sixteens at 158%, Escape restores. Walk passes end to end, five runs.

second adversarial review, on the built thing. Fixed while here: the snap guide never drew while placing (the guide path bails when no layer is selected) so a catch was invisible, and the marker was drawn ABOVE the guide so the yellow was hidden; the mode now takes the keyboard on entry so the arrow keys work straight after a menu or panel press; hover and the pointer are taken over so nothing on the canvas lights up. Left rough and filed in the audit: no dot at the crossing, no hint when the zero point is off screen, and the arrow keys belong to the slider once you have touched it.

Grid gains a zero point you place on the canvas (two accent lines, press to move, arrows to nudge 1pt/10pt, catching layer and canvas edges through the same Snapping call a layer drag makes, tool bar replaced by a Cancel/Done/smallest cell bar, Return keeps and Escape restores) and a smallest cell that floors what the grid draws at any zoom while the pull stays on the typed spacing. Core is TDD (21 new tests, 3327 green); verified live on the probe with Scripts/playtest/grid-origin-walk.json and real screen captures; audit at queue/audits/2026-09-05-grid-origin.json. Shipped in fa64398, pushed to main.
